## Comparability check

All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1–Dec 31), so the FY2023 vs. FY2024 periods line up directly [DOC-1]. One caveat: the excerpt does not disclose whether any of the FY2024 figures include acquired operations, so high revenue-growth readings (notably Alaska's) cannot be confirmed as purely organic from this source. "Strongest performer" is also not defined in the source, so I evaluate it on scale, profitability (operating margin), and year-over-year improvement.

## FY2024 metrics (derived from [DOC-1])

| Airline | FY24 Revenue | FY24 Op. income | FY24 Op. margin | FY23 Op. margin | Rev. growth | Op. income growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $61,643M | $5,995M | 9.7% | 9.5% | +6.2% | +8.6% |
| United | $57,063M | $5,096M | 8.9% | 7.8% | +6.2% | +21.0% |
| Southwest | $27,483M | $321M | 1.2% | 0.9% | +5.3% | +43.3% |
| American | $54,211M | $2,614M | 4.8% | 5.7% | +2.7% | −13.8% |
| Alaska | $11,735M | $570M | 4.9% | 3.8% | +12.6% | +44.7% |

Supporting figures: Delta revenue $58,048M → $61,643M and operating income $5,521M → $5,995M [DOC-1]; United revenue $53,717M → $57,063M and operating income $4,211M → $5,096M [DOC-1]; Southwest revenue $26,091M → $27,483M and operating income $224M → $321M [DOC-1]; American revenue $52,788M → $54,211M and operating income $3,034M → $2,614M [DOC-1]; Alaska revenue $10,426M → $11,735M and operating income $394M → $570M [DOC-1].

## Assessment

- **Delta** posted both the largest operating income ($5,995M) and the highest operating margin (9.7%) of the group, and grew both revenue and operating income [DOC-1].
- **United** was the closest competitor and had the better *improvement* story among the large carriers: +21.0% operating income growth and ~109 bps of margin expansion, versus Delta's ~21 bps [DOC-1].
- **Alaska** and **Southwest** show the highest percentage growth rates, but off very small profit bases ($394M and $224M in FY2023), and their FY2024 margins (4.9% and 1.2%) remain far below Delta's [DOC-1].
- **American** was the clear laggard — the only carrier with declining operating income (−13.8%) and contracting margin, plus the slowest revenue growth (+2.7%) [DOC-1].

On absolute profitability and margin — the most standard measures of airline performance — Delta wins; if the criterion is rate of improvement, United (large-cap) or Alaska (percentage terms, subject to the organic-growth caveat) would lead.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — it was the strongest FY2024 performer on the most meaningful measures, with the highest operating income ($5,995M) and the highest operating margin (9.7%), while growing revenue 6.2% and operating income 8.6%; United ranks a close second (best margin expansion among the large carriers, +109 bps), and American was the weakest (only carrier with declining operating income, −13.8%).
